p1.original: 10.1 人格是由生物学因素、情境和心理过程共同塑造的，这些过程都发生在一定的社会文化和个体成长的背景中。
p1.en: 10.1 The personality is shaped by biological factors, circumstances and psychological processes that take place in a context of social culture and individual growth.

p2.original: 10.2 所有特质理论都会提出某些人格特征（如气质、特质或人格类型），这些特征会使人们的人格随时间的流逝保持稳定不变。
p2.en: 10.2 All qualitative theories suggest certain personality characteristics (e.g., quality, quality or type of personality) that can keep the human personality stable at any time.

p3.original: 10.3 尽管每一种人格过程理论都强调人格发展过程中的不同塑造力量，但是也都会把人格描述为内部心理过程和社会交互的结果。
p3.en: 10.3 While each personality process theory emphasizes different shaping forces in the process of personality development, personality is also described as the result of internal psychological processes and social interactions.

p4.original: 10.4 我们对自己和他人的了解是以内隐人格理论和自我叙述为基础的，这两者都受到社会文化的影响。
p4.en: 10.4 Our understanding of ourselves and others is based on the theory of hidden personality and self-presentation, both of which are influenced by social and cultural factors.

p5.original: 你认为自己是独一无二的吗？

p7.original: 根据你的自我意识和立场，你能经常预测你在未来一周或一年中会做什么或不会做什么吗？
p7.en: Based on your self-consciousness and position, can you often predict what you will or will not do in the coming week or year?

p8.original: 你的亲朋好友是不是都认为在不同情境中你也能行为如一，可以预测？
p8.en: Does your family and friends think you can behave in different situations, predictable?

p9.original: 大多数人都认为，基因、性格与人格特质等内在决定因素共同构成了核心自我，从而决定了人们常见的行为。实际上，我们几乎不会怀疑这样的假设：我们每个人都是独特的个体，都有独一无二的自我使自己与众不同。但是，我们是怎样成为一个独特个体的呢？
p9.en: Most people believe that the underlying determinants of genes, character and personality form the core self together, thus shaping common behaviour. In fact, we hardly doubt the assumption that each of us is a unique individual and that each of us has a unique self-proclaimed identity. But how did we become a unique individual?

p10.original: 有趣的是，这个问题之所以扎根于心理学之中完全是因为一个非凡的女学者。她在不接纳她的男性世界中为了成为自己而终身努力奋斗。她的最高追求是什么呢？她曾在男性主导的学术界中因为自己的女性性别而被排斥，因此她只是简单地想让学术界认可她是一个有能力的学者（Calkins，1906，1930；DiFebo，2002）。
p10.en: Interestingly, the problem is rooted in psychology only because of an extraordinary female scholar. She struggled for her life to become herself in a male world that did not accept her. What's her supreme pursuit? She has been excluded from male-dominated academia because of her gender, and she simply wants to have her recognition as a capable scholar (Calkins, 1906, 1930); DiFebo, 2002.

p11.original: 玛丽·卡尔金斯（Mary Calkins）是以非正式的方式进入心理学领域的。19世纪晚期，美国女校韦尔斯利学院授予她杰出教师的荣誉，并给她提供了在当时的新兴学科——心理学领域的一个工作机会，但前提是她要进修心理学（这在当时的女子学院实属罕见）。然而，在当时，找到一所愿意接收女生的研究生院很难。但韦尔斯利学院附近的哈佛大学为她提供了机会，著名的心理学先驱威廉·詹姆斯愿意收她为学生。唯一的难题是哈佛大学当时不招收女学生。当时的校长查尔斯·艾略特（Charles Eliot）强烈主张男女学生应该分开接受教育。但是，在詹姆斯和心理学系其他学者的压力下，他的态度有所缓和，妥协条件是玛丽·卡尔金斯只能参加非正式的课程，而且永远没有资格获得哈佛大学的博士学位（哈佛大学直到1963年才授予女性博士学位）。
p11.en: Mary Calkins has entered the field of psychology informally. In the late nineteenth century, the Wellsley College of American Girls awarded her the honour of a distinguished teacher and offered her a job in the field of psychology, a new subject at the time, provided that she was pursuing psychology (which was rare at the time at the Girls' College). However, it was difficult at that time to find a graduate school willing to accept girls. But Harvard University, near Wellsley College, provided her with an opportunity, and William James, the famous pioneer of psychology, offered her as a student. The only problem was that Harvard didn't admit female students at that time. Charles Elliot, the then headmaster, strongly advocated separate education for boys and girls. However, under pressure from James and other scholars in the Department of Psychology, his attitude was tempered by a compromise that Mary Carlkins would only attend informal courses and would never qualify for a doctorate from Harvard University (Horph University did not award a doctorate to women until 1963).

p12.original: 因此，卡尔金斯开始了她在哈佛大学的研究生课程学习，直到1895年春天她才学完了所有的课程。她还完成了她的博士学位论文《联想：分析和实验》（Association: An Essay Analytic and Experimental），这是一项有关记忆方面的开创性研究。她设计了配对联想记忆测验，后来成为记忆研究领域的标准。为了全力支持她的工作，具有反抗精神的哈佛大学心理学教师们让她进行了非官方的论文答辩，并提议哈佛大学学位委员会授予她博士学位。威廉·詹姆斯称赞她的表现是“哈佛有史以来最出色的博士答辩”。但令人惊讶的是，委员会拒绝了。被激怒的威廉·詹姆斯告诉卡尔金斯，哈佛大学的行为“足以把包括你在内的所有女性都变成引爆者”（Furumoto，1979，p.350）。然而，卡尔金斯并没有诋毁这所大学，她毕生坚持不懈地学习、研究和写作。
p12.en: As a result, Carlkins began her postgraduate studies at Harvard University, and she did not complete all her courses until the spring of 1895. She also completed her doctorate thesis " Convergence: Analysis and Experiments " (Association: An Essay Analytic and Experimental), a groundbreaking study on memory. She designed a twin vision memory test, which later became a standard in the field of memory research. In order to fully support her work, the resistance teachers at Harvard University gave her an unofficial dissertation and proposed that the Harvard University Degrees Committee award her a doctorate. William James praised her performance as “Harvard's most outstanding doctoral response ever”. It was surprising, however, that the Committee had rejected it. The angry William James told Carlkins that Harvard's behaviour “is enough to turn all women, including you, into triggerers” (Furumoto, 1979, p. 350). However, Carlkins did not denigrate the university, which she has been studying, researching and writing for the rest of her life.

p13.original: 尽管没有获得博士学位，玛丽·卡尔金斯还是按照之前的承诺回到了韦尔斯利学院担任心理学教师。作为一名高产的学者和敬业的教师，她一生发表了100多篇文章、出版了4部著作，其中包括最畅销的教科书《心理学导论》（An Introductaion to Psychology）。在韦尔斯利学院，她帮助组建了美国早期的心理学实验室之一。玛丽还开创了两个心理学领域：梦的解析（后来得到了弗洛伊德的认可）和自我心理学（她的主要研究兴趣）。1905年，她成为美国心理学会第一位女主席，后来又成为美国哲学学会第一位女主席。在她乐观向上的自传中，玛丽感恩在一生中从同事那里得到的所有帮助。虽然她的成就足以让她赢得尊重，但她从未鄙视过那些拒绝尊重她及其成就的人。玛丽·卡尔金斯于1930年去世，享年67岁。
p13.en: Despite the absence of a doctorate, Mary Carkins returned to the Wellsley College as a psychologist, in accordance with previous commitments. As a highly productive scholar and professional teacher, she has published more than 100 articles and four books throughout her life, including the best-selling textbook An Institute to Psychology. At Wellsley College, she helped to form one of the early psychology laboratories in the United States. Mary also initiated two areas of psychology: dream analysis (which was later recognized by Freud) and self-psychology (whose main research interests were). In 1905, she became the first woman president of the American Psychological Association and later the first woman president of the American Philosophy Society. In her optimistic autobiography, Mary is grateful for all the help she has received from her colleagues throughout her life. While her achievements were sufficient to earn her respect, she had never despised those who refused to respect her and her achievements. Mary Carkins died in 1930 and was 67 years old.

p14.original: 人格是跨越时间和生活情境的一致性倾向
p14.en: Personality is a tendency to be consistent across time and life situations.

p15.original: 尽管在整个职业生涯中遭遇的障碍重重，玛丽·卡尔金斯还是坚持不懈地学习和追求成功。她的这种动机和行为模式很好地反映了本章的主题。人格（personality）包括使个体跨时间和情境的行为保持连续性的所有心理品质和过程。这个概念很宽泛，我们也可以将其描述为贯穿我们人生的一致性倾向（Cervone & Shoda，1999）。如果这种一致性倾向被破坏，可能会导致一个人产生不一致性的人格，如精神分裂症或分离性身份障碍（曾被称为多重人格障碍）等人格障碍或极端的精神问题。人格心理学家面临的难题是，需要将个体的方方面面有机地整合在一起。这是一个试图把人作为一个整体来理解的整合过程，以便把对人类思想、情感和行为（包括学习、知觉、发展、动机、情绪及其他心理过程等）至关重要的一切整合起来。
p15.en: Despite the many obstacles encountered throughout her career, Mary Carlkins has continued to learn and pursue success. Her motivations and patterns of behaviour reflect the subject of this chapter well. Personality includes all psychological qualities and processes that enable the conduct of individuals across time and circumstances to remain continuous. The concept is broad and we can describe it as a convergence trend that runs through our lives (Cervone & Shoda, 1999). If this tendency towards consistency is undermined, it may result in the creation of inconsistent personality problems, such as schizophrenia or separability (formerly referred to as multiple personality disorders), or extreme mental problems. The challenge for personality psychologists is to integrate the various aspects of the individual in an organic way. It is an integration process that seeks to understand the human person as a whole in order to integrate everything that is essential to human thinking, emotions and behaviour, including learning, consciousness, development, motivation, emotions and other psychological processes.

p16.original: 在某些方面，人格很简单，因为我们在某些方面都很相似。我们通常喜欢快乐而不是痛苦，有时会感到兴奋，对千篇一律感到厌烦，追求生活的意义，经常以他人的行为标准来评价自己。但除了这些明显的相似性之外，我们每个人又是独一无二的个体，即每个人都与他人不同。就像世界上数十亿人没有完全相同的指纹一样，两个人也没有完全相同的人格，即使是双胞胎也有不同之处。因此，人格也是个体差异的心理学，即研究什么让我们的思维、感受和行为在相同情境下与众不同。当我们研究这个问题时，我们将用玛丽·卡尔金斯的故事来说明人格心理学家是如何试图洞察这个有趣的过程的。
p16.en: In some respects, the personality is simple, because we are very similar in some respects. We usually like happiness rather than pain, sometimes excited, tired of everything, pursuing the meaning of life and often judging ourselves by the standards of behaviour of others. But in addition to these obvious similarities, each of us is a unique individual, that is, each is different from the other. Just as billions of people in the world do not have identical fingerprints, two people do not have identical personalities, even twins. Personality is therefore also the psychology of individual differences, that is, the study of what makes our thinking, feelings and behaviour different in the same context. As we look at this issue, we will use the story of Mary Carlkins to show how the personality psychologist tried to see this interesting process.

p17.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p18.original: 是什么力量塑造了玛丽·卡尔金斯人格中表现出来的独特行为模式、高成就动机、跨时空一致性和应对压力的坚韧性？
p18.en: What power has shaped the unique pattern of behaviour displayed by Mary Carlkins in her personality, the high motivation for achievement, the consistency across time and space and the resilience to stress?

p19.original: 玛丽的人格是由其身边的人和生活中的事情塑造的吗？由于这些外在因素经常超出她的控制，我们必须考虑另一种可能性：她的勇气和决断更多的是来自内在特质，即她的基本人格，包括她的价值观、态度、工作习惯和自强倾向。你可能会把内在和外在这两个相对宽泛的概念看作发展心理学中非常重要的先天和后天基本问题的另一个变式。当然，答案是两者都起作用：经验和先天因素塑造了玛丽·卡尔金斯的人格，就像它们也塑造了你和我的人格一样。本章将介绍几种人格理论，即关于人格是什么、它如何发展和如何产生作用的理论解释。跟随本章学习，你会发现一些理论更强调先天，而另一些则更重视后天养育。你还会发现某个理论只适合处理某种特定类型的人格问题。下面是几个例子。
p19.en: Is Mary's personality shaped by the people around her and the things in her life? Since these externalities often exceed her control, we must consider another possibility: her courage and determination come more from the intrinsic traits of her fundamental personality, including her values, attitudes, working habits and self-empowerment. You may view these two relatively broad concepts, both internal and external, as yet another variant of the basic issues of developing the fundamental issues of birth and nate. Of course, the answer is that both work: experience and congenital factors shape Mary Carlkins' personality, just as they shape yours and mine. This chapter will present several personality theories, namely theoretical interpretations of what the personality is, how it develops and how it works. Learning from this chapter, you will find some theories that place greater emphasis on birth and others on rearing. And you'll find that a theory is only appropriate for dealing with a particular type of personality. Below are a few examples.

p20.original: 如果你所需要的是对他人当前人格特征的印象（如当你为公司筛选求职者时），那么气质、特质或类型理论可能是你最好的选择。
p20.en: If what you need is an impression of the current personality of another person (e.g. when you screen a job seeker for a company), the theory of quality, quality or type may be your best choice.

p21.original: 如果你的目标是了解一个正在成长和改变的人（如一位向你寻求建议的朋友或者退伍老兵），你可能会发现心理动力学、人本主义、存在主义或社会认知理论最有帮助。
p21.en: If your goal is to understand a person who is growing and changing (e.g. a friend or veteran who seeks advice from you), you may find psychodynamic, humanistic, existential or social cognitive theories most helpful.

p22.original: 如果人们如何相互理解是你最感兴趣的话题（当你在做婚姻咨询或冲突管理时），你可能希望知道人们对彼此的看法，也就是说，你要了解他们的内隐人格理论。
p22.en: If people understand each other (when you're doing marriage counseling or conflict management), you might want to know what people think about each other, that is, what their hidden personality theory is.

p23.original: 如果你要了解人们是否以相同的方式理解周围的世界，你会希望了解跨文化人格研究。这类研究融入整章的内容中。
p23.en: If you want to know whether people understand the world around them in the same way, you want to know about intercultural personality studies. Such research is integrated throughout the chapter.

p24.original: 现在，我们先概述各种塑造我们人格的力量，作为了解人格的起点。
p24.en: Now, let us begin by outlining the forces that shape our personality as a starting point for understanding it.
